metadata.name: Risk of Paradoxical Embolism (RoPE) Score
metadata.summary: 10-point clinical index estimating the probability that a patent foramen ovale (PFO) is causally related vs incidental in cryptogenic ischemic stroke.
clinical_pearls: Points are awarded for the ABSENCE of traditional vascular risk factors, younger age, and a cortical infarct on neuroimaging.
High RoPE scores (>= 7) indicate a high PFO-attributable fraction (72%–88%) and correlate with greater relative benefit from PFO closure in pooled trial analyses (Kent et al., 2020).

Pitfall — Suggests causality, does not prove it: A high RoPE score in cryptogenic embolic stroke strongly suggests a PFO-related mechanism but does not replace thorough exclusion of occult atrial fibrillation or large-vessel disease.

Pitfall — Do not gate echocardiography or closure alone: Should NOT be used in isolation to decide which stroke patients undergo echocardiography or which PFO patients undergo closure without anatomical risk assessment (e.g., PASCAL).

items.label: No History of Prior Stroke or TIA

interpretation.label: Very Low Probability (0–3 pts · 0% PFO-Attributable)
interpretation.summary: PFO is likely incidental; focus on conventional secondary prevention and occult AF/atherosclerosis workup.

interpretation.label: Low-to-Moderate Probability (4–5 pts · 34%–38% PFO-Attributable)
interpretation.summary: 34% (score 4) to 38% (score 5) PFO-attributable fraction; PFO is more likely incidental than causal unless high-risk anatomy is present.

interpretation.label: Moderate Probability (6 pts · 62% PFO-Attributable)
interpretation.summary: 62% PFO-attributable fraction; integrate with PASCAL high-risk PFO features (large shunt, atrial septal aneurysm).

interpretation.label: High Probability (7–8 pts · 72%–84% PFO-Attributable)
interpretation.summary: 72% (score 7) to 84% (score 8) PFO-attributable fraction; strong candidate for PFO closure evaluation after ruling out AF.

interpretation.label: Very High Probability (9–10 pts · 88% PFO-Attributable)
interpretation.summary: 88% PFO-attributable fraction; PFO is highly likely causal in this young cryptogenic stroke patient.

assessment_guides.title: Applying RoPE Score in Cryptogenic Stroke
bedside_steps: Apply only after standard stroke workup excludes large-artery atherosclerosis, cardioembolism (e.g. AF), and small-vessel lacunar disease.
pitfalls_and_exceptions: RoPE does not incorporate PFO anatomical features (atrial septal aneurysm or large right-to-left shunt); pair with PASCAL classification when deciding on PFO closure.

references.citation: Kent DM, Ruthazer R, Weimar C, et al. An index to identify stroke-related vs incidental patent foramen ovale in cryptogenic stroke. Neurology. 2013;81(7):619-625.

Prefasi D, Martínez-Sánchez P, Fuentes B, Díez-Tejedor E. The utility of the RoPE score in cryptogenic stroke patients <= 50 years in predicting a stroke-related patent foramen ovale. Int J Stroke. 2016;11(1):NP7-NP8.

Kent DM, Saver JL, Ruthazer R, et al. Risk of Paradoxical Embolism (RoPE)-Estimated Attributable Fraction Correlates With the Benefit of Patent Foramen Ovale Closure: An Analysis of 3 Trials. Stroke. 2020;51(10):3119-3123.
